issues.description: Reading the full script into the RPC payload on every compile is wrong-shape
issues.detail: The backend already wrote the file to disk and returns its path. Now it also slurps the entire script content into the JSON response so the frontend can turn around and offer a download. That's a duplicate transport of the same bytes over the RPC channel for every compile, regardless of whether the user clicks Download. Stream it on demand via a download endpoint, or read the file in the frontend from the path that's already returned.

issues.description: open() without encoding and without error handling for a file that just got written
issues.detail: open(script_path) uses the platform default encoding, which is exactly the kind of thing that bites you six months later on a non-UTF-8 locale. If the file disappears or is unreadable, the whole compile RPC now fails after compilation succeeded — the user loses the package_path they would otherwise have gotten. Either specify encoding='utf-8' and wrap it, or drop the read entirely (preferred).

issues.description: Download icon is a clickable element but not a button
issues.detail: GetAppIcon with onClick is not focusable, not keyboard-activatable, and has no role. The adjacent 'Done' link is an anchor and behaves correctly. Use an IconButton or wrap it; otherwise keyboard and screen-reader users can't trigger it. titleAccess alone doesn't fix that.

If compiledPath is empty the code writes a file named 'pipeline.kale.py' that may not match the actual pipeline name at all. The split('/').pop() also doesn't handle Windows separators if the path ever comes through unmangled. Minor, but the fallback should either fail loudly or use the pipeline name from metadata that's already in scope.

issues.description: Whole-file content shipped through React state is needlessly heavy
issues.detail: compiledContent now lives on DeployProgressState and is passed down through DeploysProgress -> DeployProgress as a prop. For large pipelines this is a multi-KB string sitting in component state forever, re-rendered on every state change, and never freed until the panel is removed. Fetching on click would avoid all of this.

review.summary: The patch does one thing — add a download button — but it does it by piping the entire compiled script through the RPC response and into React state, when the file is already on disk and its path is already returned. That's the wrong shape: shovel bytes once, on click, from a download endpoint, not on every compile through a JSON payload. The backend read is also unencoded and unguarded, so a locale or filesystem hiccup now breaks a compile that otherwise succeeded. The frontend icon is a div-with-onClick masquerading as a button — not keyboard accessible. NEEDS-WORK: split into a download endpoint (or read-from-path) plus an actual button, then resubmit.
